title: Staggered Sundown Miniroll Slate and Communication Briefing
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight ops slate for a small, staggered nighttime miniroll ("sundown") targeting low-traffic lanes. It combines a compact rollout calendar, a pragmatic preflight checklist, on-call and comm play, and a release-notes draft for customer-facing copy. Use this for small-but-sensitive feature flips where we want incremental visibility and rapid rollback capability.

High-level objectives:
- Deploy feature flags and runtime kernel swap for model-variant routing with minimal surface area.
- Validate latency and error-rate invariants under low traffic, then expand traffic windows if metrics are clean.
- Keep rollback path < 3 minutes from detection to HW/traffic adjustment.

Audience / owners:
- Release lead: Ava Patel (owner)
- Canary shepherd: Ethan Brooks
- Observability lead: Samira Khan
- Platform SRE on-call: Diego Martinez
- Production API owner: Rina Sato

Rollout calendar (local PST windows):
- 2025-11-18 21:30–21:45: Warm-up lane (0.5% traffic) — small region: us-west1, low-priority nodes
- 2025-11-18 21:50–22:10: Canary lane (2% traffic) — same region, additional node pool
- 2025-11-18 22:20–22:45: Quiet expansion (10% traffic) — add us-central1 internal lanes
- 2025-11-18 23:00–23:30: Evaluate & either promote to 50% (soft) or rollback
- Contingency hold: 23:30–00:15 — teams on standby and metrics reviewed
Note: Each step must be gate-approved by release lead and observability lead before progressing.

Preflight checklist (must be green before 21:30 start):
- [ ] Release branch built and SHA verified (CI pipeline green) — PR/987 merged
- [ ] Migration-free deploy (no schema changes) — validated by platform-engineering
- [ ] Smoke tests for core endpoints passing on staging with realistic latency (see smoke commands)
- [ ] Canary config uploaded to routing service and feature-flag entries created
- [ ] Healthcheck probes (liveness/readiness) tuned to low false positives for night windows
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned and short links shared to #release-watch and #sre-ops
- [ ] Pager rotation confirmed for on-call SRE and backup (Diego -> Rina)
- [ ] Rollback playbook reviewed and rollback token issued to release lead

Quick smoke commands (examples):
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-minisnap","prompt":"smoke test"}' | jq '.status'
- kubectl rollout status deploy/platform-api -n prod --timeout=120s

Canary gating signals (primary):
- 95th perc latency change vs baseline < +15%
- Error rate (5m) increase < 0.2% absolute and < 30% relative
- LCR (long-tail completion ratio) within expected bounds for model variant
- CPU/GPU utilization within projected headroom; no OOMs or repeated retries

Secondary signals (for manual review):
- Token-level cost spike above forecast for the 15m window
- Unusual growth in rate-limited responses or throttles
- Anomalous increase in client retry traffic (indicates degraded responses)

Rollback and mitigation matrix (fast paths):
- Severe error spike or latency regression: toggle routing to previous model variant (feature-flag rollback) — target time < 2 minutes.
- Node-level instability: remove affected node pool from routing and trigger autoscaling warm pool — target time < 5 minutes.
- Observability failure (metrics missing): hold expansion and fallback to manual sampling and console checks.
- If rollback is triggered, notify #release-ops, postmortem owner will be assigned within 24h.

Communication plan (who says what):
- T-30m: Release lead posts preflight summary to #release-watch and @oncall-sre; include pinned dashboard links and the canary fractions.
- On each step: Canary shepherd confirms step started in-thread and posts key metrics at T+5m.
- If gate passes: release lead posts approval and next window.
- If gate fails: release lead posts incident code (REL-4321) and action (rollback toggled).
- Post-roll: short digest in #all-eng with links to full release notes.

On-call and escalation (order):
1) Platform SRE on-call: Diego Martinez (primary) — pager
2) Observability lead: Samira Khan (escalation) — Slack DM + phone if unresolved 10m
3) Release lead: Ava Patel (final decision on promote/rollback)

Monitoring dashboard shortcuts (short links):
- Miniroll overview: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/miniroll/overview?org=eng&rel=REL-4321
- Latency heatmap: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/latency/miniroll
- Error waterfall: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/errors/miniroll

Release notes (draft for external/internal):
- Short external blurb (customer-facing):
  "Nighttime routing improvements: we incrementally deployed a targeted routing update to provide faster fallbacks and reduced tail latency for model variants. This update was rolled out in small stages during an overnight maintenance window and will be gradually expanded. No action required by customers."

- Internal detailed notes (for eng and SRE):
  - Deployed routing toggle to prefer rwd-13b-minisnap for short-context requests in low-traffic lanes.
  - Added conservative KV-cache warmup to reduce cold-start tail latency.
  - Smoothed kernel selection logic to prefer FP16 optimized path when memory headroom available.
  - Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/987
  - Jira: REL-4321

Risk register (quick):
- Medium: Unexpected cost increase if miniroll triggers more long completions than forecast. Mitigation: cost alert with auto-hold at 300% of window forecast.
- Low: Config drift between us-west1 and us-central1 routing tables. Mitigation: preflight double-check script and a config checksum.
- Medium: Observability mis-tags causing false negatives on gate. Mitigation: manual verification step in hold window.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add an automatic canary abort on sustained 10% latency regression (proposal for future automation)? Owner: Samira
- Add a secondary lightweight smoke that exercises embeddings route (not currently in smoke) — owner: Ethan
- Post-ship: run a 24h cost compare job between flagged users and baseline — owner: Platform FinOps

Post-release checklist (within 24h):
- [ ] Confirm final traffic split and update routing docs
- [ ] Create short postmortem if any gating failures occurred
- [ ] Close JIRA REL-4321 after QA signoff
- [ ] Update customer-facing release notes if expansion begins

Appendix: quick config verification script (example):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://control.redwood.ai/v1/configs/routing/miniroll | jq '.checksum'
- Compare checksum to the preflight value: expected: "sha256:3f4a..."

Notes to self (field rough):
- Keep the windows tight; sundown slots avoid peak EU traffic early but coordinate with infra for any cross-region warmups.
- If any step looks like it will take > 10m, hold expansion and reassess.

Document history:
- 2025-11-05: initial draft by Ava
- 2025-11-07: added rollback matrix and smoke commands (Ethan)
- 2025-11-09: observation thresholds tuned (Samira)
- 2025-11-12: comm plan and release notes draft added (Ava)

End of slate.
